podcast.title: First Female-Fronted Ska Band with Major Hit Since No Doubt
podcast.body: The Interrupters were highlighted as a significant band in the "fourth wave" of Ska, which arrived in the late 2010s. They became the first female-fronted Ska band to achieve a major hit since No Doubt, showcasing the genre's continued evolution and relevance in North America. "If you're into the scene, you might know about the steady 45s, lost agritones and of course, the interruptors." "They became the first female fronted Skaban to have a major hit since no doubt."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 4: The Revivals

podcast.title: Fourth Wave Leader
podcast.body: The Interrupters, from Los Angeles, record for Hellcat Records (a label associated with Rancid) and are considered the current leader in the fourth wave of Ska. Their success marks the first female-fronted Ska hit since No Doubt. "The biggest of them all, so far, has been the Interruptors. They're from Los Angeles and record for Hellcat Records, a label associated with, and here's that name again, Ranset. This was the first female fronted SCAT hit, since no doubt. The Interruptors, the current leader in the 4th wave of SCAT."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Growing Success in the 2010s
podcast.body: The Interrupters, a band formed in 2011, steadily gained popularity and grew bigger as the 2010s decade progressed, illustrating that new rock bands could still find success during a challenging period for the genre. "Here's a band that was formed in 2011 and just kept getting bigger as the decade wore on. It's the interrupters."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 1: Rock Struggles Again

xref.title: Female-Fronted Ska Hit
xref.body: No Doubt was responsible for the first female-fronted Ska hit until The Interrupters emerged in the fourth wave. "This was the first female fronted SCAT hit, since no doubt."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Hellcat Records Association
xref.body: The label Hellcat Records, which records The Interrupters, is associated with Rancid, highlighting the band's ongoing influence in the Ska scene. "They're from Los Angeles and record for Hellcat Records, a label associated with, and here's that name again, Ranset."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Third Wave Ska Leader
xref.body: No Doubt was a prominent band in the "third wave" of Ska, which arrived in the 1990s. This wave saw significant popularity with bands like The Mighty Mighty Bosstones, Sublime, Reel Big Fish, Goldfinger, and Dance Hall Crashers. The Interrupters were noted as the first female-fronted Ska band to have a major hit since No Doubt. "Third wave Scott arrived in the 1990s, no doubt, muddy, muddy boss tones, sublime, real big fish, gold finger, dancehall crashes and so many more." "They became the first female fronted Skaban to have a major hit since no doubt."
